page: Amazon Web Services i7i.metal-24xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processor. This x86_64 architecture system features 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz, supported by a 320 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Storage is highly dense, featuring 22500 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, while network connectivity is supported by a 56 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

In benchmark testing, the i7i.metal-24xl demonstrates top-tier performance across multiple compute and data-processing workloads. The system achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark database operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput also rank in the top tier. Memory performance is strong, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 289.55 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 119.86 GB/sec. Additionally, the processor support for Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 instructions enables strong performance in LLM inference tasks, particularly for prompt processing with medium-sized models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by combining massive local NVMe storage with a high-capacity DDR5 memory array on a bare-metal platform, reducing the virtualization overhead typically associated with multi-tenant instances. This hardware profile is highly optimized for IO-intensive and data-heavy workloads. It is best suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, high-throughput static web serving, data decompression pipelines, and localized machine learning inference tasks that benefit from AMX acceleration without requiring dedicated GPU hardware.
